en.bh1: Sit comfortably, with your back straight. Close your eyes. If you like, rest your index fingers lightly on the soft flaps of your ears.
en.bh2: Breathe in slowly through your nose. As you breathe out, hum softly with your lips closed, like a bee. Feel the gentle hum in your face and head.
en.bh3: Good. Now continue on your own, at your own pace, a few more times.
en.bh4: Now let your breath become natural. Sit still, and notice the quiet, and the calm inside you.
en.bh5: When you are ready, gently open your eyes. If you are going to sleep, lie down, and rest.

en.bh2a: Breathe in slowly through your nose. As you breathe out, hum softly with your lips closed, like a bee. Like this:
en.bh2b: Feel the gentle hum in your face and head. Now you try.
en.sb1: Lie down, or sit comfortably. Let your shoulders drop, and close your eyes if you like.
en.sb2: We will breathe slowly together. Breathe in through your nose for a count of four, and out slowly for a count of six. Let your belly go soft as you breathe out.
en.out6: And out, two, three, four, five, six.
en.sb3: Good. Keep going on your own: in for four, out for six.
en.sb4: Now a little slower. Breathe in for four, and out for eight.
en.out8: And out, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight.
en.sb5: Keep going on your own, in for four, and out for eight.
en.sb6: Now let your breath find its own pace. Notice how calm your body feels. Stay here as long as you like.
en.rl-c1: Warmth. <#0.6#> Put warmth on your lower belly: a hot water bag, or a bottle of warm water wrapped in a cloth. Warm, not hot.
en.rl-c2: Child’s pose. <#0.6#> Kneel, sit back on your heels and stretch your arms forward on the floor. Rest your forehead down and breathe slowly.
en.rl-c3: Knees to chest. <#0.6#> Lie on your back and hug your knees to your chest. Rock gently from side to side.
en.rl-c4: Slow breaths. <#0.6#> Breathe in for 4, and out for 6. Let your belly go soft each time you breathe out.
en.rl-n1: Fresh air. <#0.6#> Open a window or step outside for a moment. Loosen anything tight around your waist.
en.rl-n2: Small sips. <#0.6#> Take small, slow sips of cool water, or coconut water or nimbu pani if you like them.
en.rl-n3: Something plain. <#0.6#> If you can, eat a little something dry and plain, like a few biscuits, khakhra or roasted chana. An empty stomach can make nausea worse.
en.rl-n4: Slow breaths. <#0.6#> Sit comfortably. Breathe in through your nose for 4, and out through your mouth for 6.
en.rl-s1: Get comfortable. <#0.6#> Lie down and dim the light. When this ends, put the phone away, face down.
en.rl-s2: Long breaths out. <#0.6#> Breathe in for 4, and out slowly for 6. Longer breaths out help many people settle.
en.rl-s3: Let go, part by part. <#0.6#> Squeeze your toes for 5 seconds, then let go. Do the same with your legs, your hands, then your shoulders.
en.rl-s4: Park your thoughts. <#0.6#> If thoughts keep coming, tell yourself: I can think about this tomorrow. Writing it in your diary note can help.
en.rl-s5: A mantra or prayer, if you like. <#0.6#> Chant softly, or in your mind: Om, the Gayatri mantra, the Hanuman Chalisa, or any prayer or devotional mantra you like. When thoughts come, gently go back to it.
en.rl-m1: Feel your feet. <#0.6#> Press your feet into the floor. Name 5 things you can see and 3 things you can hear.
en.rl-m2: Box breathing. <#0.6#> Breathe in for 4, hold for 4, out for 4, hold for 4. Then again, slowly.
en.rl-m3: A kind word. <#0.6#> Put a hand on your chest and tell yourself: this is hard, and it will pass.
en.rl-m4: One small step. <#0.6#> Pick one small thing for the next hour: a glass of water, a short walk, or a call to someone you trust.
en.rl-h1: Cool down. <#0.6#> Loosen your clothes or take off a layer. Splash cool water on your face and wrists.
en.rl-h2: Sip something cool. <#0.6#> Sip cool water slowly. For some women hot tea or spicy food sets off flushes; notice what does it for you.
en.rl-h3: Slow breathing. <#0.6#> Breathe slowly: in for 5, out for 5. Tell yourself: this will pass in a few minutes, I can let it pass. Keep going until the heat passes.

hi.bh1: पीठ सीधी रखकर आराम से बैठें। आँखें बंद करें। चाहें तो तर्जनी उँगलियाँ हल्के से कानों के नरम हिस्से पर रखें।
hi.bh2: नाक से धीरे-धीरे साँस लें। साँस छोड़ते हुए, होंठ बंद रखकर, भौंरे की तरह धीरे से गुनगुनाएँ। चेहरे और सिर में हल्की-सी गूँज महसूस करें।
hi.bh3: बहुत अच्छा। अब अपनी गति से, कुछ बार और ऐसे ही करें।
hi.bh4: अब साँस को सहज होने दें। शांत बैठें, और भीतर की शांति महसूस करें।
hi.bh5: जब मन करे, धीरे से आँखें खोलें। अगर सोने जा रही हैं, तो लेट जाएँ, और आराम करें।
hi.yn1: पीठ के बल लेट जाएँ। हाथ शरीर के पास रखें, हथेलियाँ ऊपर की ओर, और पैरों को धीरे से थोड़ा खुला छोड़ दें। आँखें बंद करें। अगले कुछ मिनट, कोशिश करें कि शरीर स्थिर रहे।
hi.yn2: धीरे से एक लंबी साँस लें, <#2#> और छोड़ दें। <#2#> फिर से, धीरे से साँस लें, <#2#> और छोड़ें। <#2#> शरीर को बिस्तर पर भारी होने दें।
hi.yn3: अब अपने लिए एक छोटी, अच्छी इच्छा सोचें। जैसे: मुझे अच्छी नींद आएगी। या: मैं शांत और स्वस्थ हूँ। अपनी इच्छा को मन में तीन बार दोहराएँ।
hi.yn4: अब मैं शरीर के जिस हिस्से का नाम लूँ, वहाँ ध्यान ले जाएँ। बस उसे महसूस करें, और आगे बढ़ें। जागती रहें, और सुनती रहें।

hi.yn12: अब महसूस करें कि शरीर हल्का हो रहा है। रुई जैसा हल्का। जैसे तैर रहा हो।

hi.rl-n1: ताज़ी हवा। <#0.6#> खिड़की खोलें या थोड़ी देर बाहर निकलें। कमर पर कुछ कसा हो तो ढीला कर लें।
